research_question: At fixed original weights, how do query-edge masking and f16 change batch scores and gradients; does local radial compression imply exact gradient death?

conclusion.mask_path_sensitivity: Full-neighborhood mean BCE increases in all four fixed batches; masked f16 mean differences are smaller, with mixed replicate signs.
conclusion.local_compression: Second-layer radial squash has substantially smaller radial than tangential Jacobian coefficients; this is a local parameterization measurement.
conclusion.gradient_zeros: All observed zero node gradient norms lie outside the batch loss structural support; every supported node has a strictly positive recorded norm in all 144 layer/cell partitions.
conclusion.generalization_root_cause: Not established; training-batch sensitivity is not valid ranking or a retraining comparison.

count_basis.cohorts: Fixed unmasked positive parent/child degree; five scored records inherit their positive group cohort
count_basis.structural_partition: Reverse both actual aggregation plans from every query endpoint, with self fallback only for empty rows; 144 partitions are repeated observations, not 144 independent networks

provenance.source_binding: Caller-declared commit corroborated by release archive and 13 LF source hashes; extracted runtime had no .git directory

limitations: Full parameter gradient vectors were not archived: norms/zero fractions are record-consistency and count checks, not independently recomputed gradients.
Full u/dLdu vectors were not archived: node norms/directional components are stored observations; mathematical consistency and their summaries are independently recomputed.
Features/checkpoint weights/all prepared tensors are not opened: per-condition input hashes and weight invariance are recorded provenance, not independent tensor rehashing.
Plain points/logits/parameter gradients were not archived: equivalence status/tolerances and necessary maximum-difference bounds are verified from records, not replayed elementwise.
NumPy does not replay PyTorch CPU randperm: sampling seed formulas, plan hashes, membership/size/order and historical batch hashes are checked, not the actual random draws.
Possible structural support is an upper bound: zero gradients inside it can reflect head activation, cancellation or other effects and do not identify gradient death.

interpretation_limits: Unmasked training queries expose target edges: lower training BCE is not a valid gain and is not a reason to remove masking.
Two selected fixed models and two preregistered batches per model; eight sampling replicates are exploratory, with no new confirmatory p-values.
Same sampling seed in two graphs does not imply identical edges or perfect common random numbers.
Local radial/tangential coefficients relative to Euclidean u do not measure complete-network conditioning, Riemannian gradients, anchor-relative drift or semantic hierarchy collapse.
Strictly positive gradient norms do not rule out small or ineffective gradients, other batches or other training stages.
Higher-degree validation-group performance gaps and training-query path sensitivities are different evidence; no causal decomposition of the MLP gap is claimed.
